transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

No, that almost probably isn't a fault, and there's no reason to send it back for this. Around 3.5 hours is completely normal for Eco 40-60 on modern machines, AEG included. That programme is the one used for the energy label, so it's designed to save energy, not time. It heats the water less and makes up for it with a longer wash and more soaking, which gets the same result as a hotter, shorter wash for a fraction of the electricity. Your old machine's hour-long 40 wash was a different kind of programme that heated harder and faster. The time on the display also isn't fixed. The machine weighs the load and checks foam and balance as it goes, so the countdown can change, often dropping with a small load. 1. Use the Cottons programme at 40°C instead of Eco 40-60. It will usually be noticeably shorter, though it uses more energy.
2. Look for a time-saving or quick option on the panel. Many AEGs have one that shortens Cottons and Synthetics cycles, and there's normally a short quick-wash programme for lightly soiled loads.
3. For everyday mixed loads that aren't very dirty, a 30°C or quick programme is often all you need. - The countdown keeps going back up or resetting over and over.
• An error code appears.
• The washing comes out cold on a genuine 60°C Cottons wash. Any of those would be a warranty matter for AEG or the retailer, so don't try to repair it yourself. One quick question to be sure: does the Eco 40-60 cycle actually finish at roughly the time it showed, or does it overrun or keep resetting?
Yes, it finishes and spins fine, and it takes about the time it showed. No error codes, and the clothes come out clean. I just wanted to be sure 3.5 hours wasn't wrong for a new machine.

That all points the same way: your machine is behaving exactly as it should. A cycle that finishes on time, spins properly, shows no error and gives clean washing is a healthy machine. 3.5 hours on Eco 40-60 is normal for a new machine, not a sign of a fault, so there's no need to send it back. The long time is deliberate. Eco 40-60 is built to use as little electricity as possible, and the time is the price of that saving. It isn't something wearing in or settling down. A couple of things that may help you live with it:
1. Keep Eco 40-60 for loads that aren't urgent, or start it with the delay timer so it finishes when you're up or home.
2. When you need a load done quicker, the Cottons or quick options mentioned earlier are the ones to use. The only things that would change my view are the ones listed before: the countdown repeatedly resetting, an error code, or cold washing on a genuine 60°C Cottons wash. If any of those ever happen while it's new, that's one for AEG or the retailer under warranty. Otherwise, enjoy the new machine.
